Job Description:

Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance / Head of Business Planning & Governance

***English job description follows***

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en gestion de programme/projet, vous souhaitez travailler dans l’environnement du service à la clientèle au sein d’une équipe dynamique et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance pour rejoindre notre équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec toute l’organisation de Service à la Clientèle pour supporter les opérateurs A220.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte qui est chargée d’assurer une exploitation sûre et économique de la flotte A220 en service. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale de manière autonome, en se soutenant mutuellement et en apprenant collectivement.

Relevant du Chef Efficacité de la flotte en service A220, vous contribuerez à la mission fondamentale de l'équipe qui consiste à garantir une exploitation efficace, sûre et économique de la flotte Airbus A220 en service, tout en améliorant en permanence la satisfaction des clients.

Vous travaillerez sur la gestion de la gouvernance des services clients A220 et soutiendrez précisément la performance de la résolution des principaux problèmes en service de la flotte A220.

Votre environnement de travail:

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce que nous prenons soin de vous :

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride, une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais et service médical sur site.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos défis:

Piloter la performance opérationnelle et économique de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service et la gouvernance globale de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 en menant les activités transverses suivantes :
Diriger les instances majeures de gouvernance :
Gouvernance MISP / SISP (Major / Significant In-Service Problems) : Assurer le pilotage de la performance de résolution des problèmes majeurs en service, le suivi du calendrier, la gestion des risques et des coûts, la coordination transversale avec l’Ingénierie et les Opérations en service, et la visibilité mensuelle aux clients avec escalade si nécessaire jusqu'au comité exécutif
Comité d'Arbitrage et de Décision du Portefeuille “Amélioration de la satisfaction client” : Structurer et animer la gouvernance d'arbitrage budgétaire et de sélection des projets (validation des business cases, ROI flotte, critères de sévérité, arbitrages et capacité d'exécution).

Coordonner la définition des indicateurs de performance (KPI) pour l'ensemble de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 et garantir leur parfait alignement avec les Top Objectifs Compagnie (TCO/TFO) A220.
Consolider, analyser et rapporter les performances mensuelles de l'entité, et intégrer ces données dans les plateformes de suivi Airbus pour assurer une visibilité transverse complète entre les différents programmes.
Coordonner la sécurité et la navigabilité de la flotte en service en monitorant les campagnes d'actions de modification et d'amélioration en cours d'exécution.
Optimiser les processus internes de gouvernance, garantir l'adhérence aux standards de l'entreprise et déployer la démarche d'Excellence Opérationnelle.
Préparer l'avenir en pilotant la stratégie de transformation, d'évolution du portefeuille de projets transverses et de régionalisation de l'équipe en soutien direct de la proximité client.

Superviser la planification financière globale (AOP - Annual Operating Plan), la gestion du compte de résultat (ABS P&L) et la gestion des risques et opportunités pour l'ensemble des Services à la Clientèle A220.
Gérer les business cases, le suivi des dépenses et les provisions budgétaires des campagnes majeures de modification d'avions (Aircraft Retrofit), représentant un budget de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars
Assumer le rôle de responsable du portefeuille (Portfolio Leader) de projets d'amélioration de la satisfaction client, avec la responsabilité complète de l'enveloppe budgétaire annuelle et des arbitrages stratégiques.
Développer la maturité en gestion de projet au sein de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service, incluant le déploiement de méthodologies, d'outils structurants et de compétences en leadership.

Votre profil:

Diplôme en ingénierie ou gestion de projet;
Minimum de quinze (15) ans d'expérience dans l'ingénierie, l'exploitation d'aéronefs ou la gestion de programmes, avec un minimum de cinq (5) ans dans un rôle de gestion;
Démontre de solides compétences en gestion de projet/programme, y compris en approche agile;
Solide sens financier spécifique à Airbus Canada et expérience souhaitable dans la gestion d'importants projets multidisciplinaires et de budgets à forte valeur;
Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, de présentation et de communication pour interagir à tous les niveaux de la direction, y compris la capacité à faire des présentations aux cadres supérieurs (Executives) et aux clients;
Est à l'aise dans des écosystèmes complexes et a une compréhension des organisations axées sur la gestion de programmes;
Est orienté(e) processus et a de l'expérience dans l'intégration de nouvelles méthodes de travail;
Promeut le travail d'équipe et agit avec leadership;
Est axé sur le client et fait preuve d'intégrité en tout temps, sans compromis;
Fait preuve d'innovation, d'engagement et de persévérance;
Une expérience en Airbus et/ou A220 et/ou en services à la clientèle est un atout certain.

En raison du secteur d’activité (aéronautique), de multiples contacts avec des entités Airbus situées dans le monde entier, et d’interactions avec les fournisseurs et clients également situés dans le monde entier, la connaissance de l’anglais est demandée dans ce poste.

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

Do you have experience in program/project management, are you interested in working in the customer services environment in a dynamic team and would you like to progress and develop new skills? Then this job is for you!

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is looking for a Head of Business Planning & Governance to join our Fleet Efficiency in-service team based in Mirabel (Québec, Canada), where you will work jointly with our Customer Services organization to support the A220 operators.

You will be working on the management of the governance of the A220 Customer Services and precisely supporting the performance of the resolution of the major in-service issues of the A220 fleet.

Your working environment:

The A220 commercial aircraft Programme is headquartered in Mirabel, in the greater Montreal area, where the vibrant city of Montreal is just a stone’s throw away. Known for its peaceful and safe environment, the region offers a high quality of life for younger or experienced professionals and families, perfectly balancing career opportunities and outdoor activities that makes it a truly special place to call home.

How we care for you:

Financial rewards: Attractive salary, annual bonus, group insurance plan, pension plan and share purchase plan.
Work / Life Balance: A hybrid working policy, on-site cafeterias and a highly competitive holiday policy.
Wellbeing/Health: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Discount Program and on-site Medical Service.
Individual development: Great upskilling opportunities and development prospects with unlimited access to +10.000 e-learning courses to develop your employability, certifications, accelerated development programmes, national and international mobility.

Your challenges:

Steer the operational and economic performance of the In-Service Fleet Efficiency team and the overall governance of the A220 Customer Services organization by leading the following transverse activities:
Lead major governance bodies:
MISP / SISP (Major / Significant In-Service Problems) Governance: Ensure the resolution performance steering of major in-service problems, schedule monitoring, risk and cost management, transverse coordination with Engineering and In-Service Operations, and monthly visibility to customers with escalation if needed up to the Executive Committee

Coordinate the definition of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the entire A220 Customer Services organization and ensure their alignment with A220 Top Company Objectives (TCO/TFO).
Consolidate, analyze, and report monthly entity performance, and integrate these data into Airbus tracking platforms to ensure complete cross-programme visibility.
Coordinate safety and airworthiness of the in-service fleet by monitoring ongoing modification and improvement action campaigns.
Optimize internal governance processes, ensure adherence to company standards, and deploy Operational Excellence practices.

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Data Governance to lead enterprise-wide data governance programs that improve data quality, regulatory compliance, business trust, and operational excellence. This leader will define and execute governance strategies across data governance, metadata management, data cataloging, data quality, master data management, and data lineage capabilities.

The Director will partner with business, technology, risk, compliance, and data leaders to establish governance frameworks, standards, policies, and controls that support data-driven decision making and regulatory requirements. Drive adoption and optimization of data governance and data catalog platforms.
Establish and oversee data quality, metadata management, master data, and data lineage programs.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, Security, and Audit teams to ensure regulatory compliance and governance readiness.
Develop governance metrics, data health KPIs, and executive reporting for senior leadership.

Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders.
Experience defining governance policies, standards, KPIs, and reporting frameworks.

Master's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.
Experience supporting regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceutical, financial services, or insurance.
Knowledge of data governance platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, or similar tools.

Knowledge of data privacy regulations, governance controls, and risk management frameworks.
Experience leading enterprise-wide data transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication and organizational change management capabilities.
Relevant certifications related to data governance, data management, privacy, or cloud technologies.

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

When it comes to health, we’re always looking for ways to push for better. It’s why we were founded in the first place. In 1957, our founder, pharmacist William Wilkinson, witnessed a mother sacrifice her health by forgoing her own medicine to pay for her sick daughter’s prescription. He knew there had to be a better way. So, he introduced North America’s first prepaid drug plan, and GreenShield was born as a non-profit with a mission to support better health for all Canadians.
We aren’t just a health and benefits company. We’re the only non-profit social enterprise that brings worlds of coverage and care together, all in one place.
We’re noble challengers, purposefully building a better way and we need the best people to help us create a more holistic approach that takes care of the mind and body.

Our mission is to create better health for all Canadians, and we know that starts with our employees.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

The Director, Finance Business Partner is a senior strategic advisor accountable for shaping financial performance, decision quality, and value creation across the Payer portfolio, including Insurance, Benefits Administration, Third Party Administration, and Claims Adjudication. Operating at the intersection of strategy, performance, and finance, this role partners closely with the EVP and senior leaders to frame decisions, challenge assumptions, assess trade-offs, and align priorities to enterprise objectives.

The role brings an enterprise-wide, forward-looking perspective—connecting pricing, claims trends, margin, cost, risk, and reinsurance considerations to strategic choices and performance outcomes.

Success in the role requires strong business judgment, influence, and the ability to translate complex financial and insurance insights into clear actions, accountability, and measurable outcomes. Success is measured through stronger decision support, improved financial and insurance performance, earlier visibility to risk and opportunity, and sustained performance improvement across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Advisory & Decision Support

Serve as a trusted advisor to the EVP and senior leaders, shaping decisions through insight, challenge, and clear articulation of trade-offs across growth, margin, cost, and risk.

Financial & Insurance Performance Leadership

Lead planning, forecasting, performance management, and business insight across the portfolio, with a strong focus on pricing, claims trends, margin drivers, cost discipline, operational efficiency, and reinsurance implications.

Performance Improvement & Value Creation

Identify and advance actions that improve performance and value realization, including business cases, scenario analysis, productivity opportunities, and disciplined follow-through on results.

Clearly define and communicate performance responsibilities, goals, expectations and objectives.

Conduct ongoing performance management activities by providing constructive feedback and coaching through regular check-ins, structured one-on-one meetings, mid-year touchpoints and annual reviews.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Scientific Director, the Manager provides operational leadership for the AGEWISE Institute and translates its scientific priorities into coordinated programs, partnerships, and deliverables. The Manager oversees day-to-day administration, research program coordination, financial planning, staff management, funding development, communications and performance reporting across the Institute’s research, implementation and education work streams.

AGEWISE brings together researchers across medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, kinesiology, engineering, fundamental and data sciences, and social sciences to advance healthy aging and translational geroscience. Its mandate connects discoveries in aging biology with clinical trials, community implementation and education to improve healthspan, function and quality of life. The Manager builds the operational infrastructure that enables this interdisciplinary work, including translational geroscience trials, research on accelerated aging after critical illness, and implementation of the AVOID frailty framework.

Job Description
Key responsibilities

1. Institute leadership, planning and governance

• Work with the Scientific Director to develop annual operational plans, budgets, milestones, and risk-management processes aligned with the Institute’s strategic priorities.
• Establish and maintain administrative systems, standard operating procedures, and a coordinated portfolio of Institute-supported activities.
• Provide secretariat support to the Steering Committee and community advisory board, including agendas, briefing materials, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Coordinate member recruitment, engagement and collaboration across faculties, Research Excellence Clusters and external partners; organize the Institute launch, member meetings and protocol-development sessions.
• Where applicable, coordinate the approved transfer of Canadian Frailty Network programs, educational resources, digital tools, contracts and residual funds to AGEWISE.

2. Translational geroscience and research operations

• Coordinate a portfolio spanning fundamental aging research, biomarkers, clinical and pragmatic trials, biomechanics, regenerative medicine, and accelerated aging in survivors of critical illness.
• Support the phased development of the proposed Clinical Trials Unit and contract research services, including feasibility planning, staffing needs, costing, workflows, and service arrangements in collaboration with existing research infrastructure.
• Work with investigators and study teams to develop projects, assess operational feasibility, coordinate participating sites, recruitment, and deliverables.
• Coordinate research ethics and other required approval processes with responsible investigators and institutional offices; maintain systems to track approvals, amendments, training and reporting deadlines.
• Facilitate agreements and processes for data sharing, and secure information management with research and institutional teams.
• Support collaborative development of common data elements and core outcomes for geroscience trials, including steering-group and Delphi-process coordination.

3. Healthy-aging implementation and community partnerships

• Oversee program coordination and deliverables for the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) -funded AVOID Frailty implementation initiative, working with the project lead and community partners.
• Build and maintain relationships with older adults, caregivers, community organizations, healthcare partners and policymakers; support meaningful involvement throughout the research cycle.
• Coordinate connections between basic scientists, engineers, and clinician scientists to advance human-ready innovations and enable access to relevant research expertise and facilities.

4. Financial management, funding and sustainability

• Develop and monitor operating and project budgets; prepare forecasts and financial reports; track commitments, expenditures and funding restrictions with institutional finance staff.
• Coordinate grant-development activities, funding calendars, investigator submissions and supporting documentation; assist with budgets, operational plans and non-scientific proposal sections.
• Administer transparent pilot-funding competitions, including calls, eligibility checks, review logistics, conflict-of-interest processes, award documentation and progress reporting.
• Support academic, industry and philanthropic partnerships with the Scientific Director and appropriate institutional offices, including contract coordination, cost recovery and contributions to Institute operations.
• Maintain a sustainability plan and ensure timely sponsor and institutional reporting.

5. People, education and knowledge mobilization

• Supervise Institute administrative and program staff assigned to the position, including recruitment, onboarding, work allocation, professional development and performance management.
• Coordinate trainee opportunities, interdisciplinary mentoring activities, educational modules and workshops in collaboration with faculty and existing academic programs.
• Organize symposia, policy roundtables and partner events; coordinate accessible website content, newsletters, public-facing materials, policy briefs and research communications with scientific contributors.
• Prepare and submit academic manuscripts of Institute’s projects as required

6. Evaluation, accountability and continuous improvement

• Maintain a dashboard of research, funding, collaboration, community engagement, training, and knowledge-mobilization indicators aligned with the proposal.
• Prepare annual reports and briefing materials for the Scientific Director, governance committees, institutional leadership, and funders.
• Identify operational risks, resource gaps and delays; recommend corrective actions and escalate issues requiring scientific or institutional decisions.
• Use feedback from members, staff, trainees, and community partners to improve Institute services and processes.

Qualifications and experience

• A doctoral degree (master’s degree a minimum) in health sciences or life sciences, research administration or a related discipline.
• At least five years of experience in research program management, preferably within a university, research institute, healthcare organization or multidisciplinary research network.
• Demonstrated experience managing budgets, grants or contracts, coordinating complex projects, and preparing reports for leadership and funders.
• Experience supervising staff and coordinating teams whose members work across disciplines or organizations.
• Working knowledge of clinical research operations, research ethics, data stewardship, and applicable institutional research requirements.
• Strong written and verbal communication, organizational and relationship-building skills, including the ability to translate complex research priorities into actionable plans.
• Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, accessible and community-engaged research practices.

Preferred assets

• Experience supporting multicentre trials, establishing research infrastructure, or coordinating academic–industry research partnerships.
• Experience with knowledge mobilization and interdisciplinary training.
• Familiarity with Canadian research funding programs and university administrative systems

Authority and working relationships

The Manager makes day-to-day operational decisions within approved plans, budgets and delegated authority, and provides recommendations on resource allocation, staffing and program development. The manager will report to the Scientific Director. The Scientific Director has responsibility and decisional authority for scientific direction, strategic priorities, institute initiatives, institute projects, and approval of major commitments.
The Manager will work closely with the Steering Committee, community advisory board, faculty members, study teams, trainees, Research Excellence Clusters, university research and finance offices, human resources, advancement and technology-transfer staff, healthcare organizations, community partners and external research networks.

jobs.description:
About KV Capital

At KV Capital, we have established ourselves as industry leaders in real estate debt and investment, driven by our unwavering commitment to excellent, trusted partnerships, and innovating solutions. We have office locations in Edmonton, Calgary, and Toronto, and continue to expand our reach nationally.

Real Estate Debt (“RED”)

Since its inception, our Real Estate Debt division has funded and/or advised on $2.5B+ of commercial deals. We provide financing solutions for land, subdivision financing, multi-family, retail, industrial, office, hospitality, mixed-use properties, and specialty financing, such as equity and structured finance deals.

Role Summary

Reporting to the Vice President, Investment Management, the Associate Director, Funding is responsible for the oversight and execution of the Funding function within the Real Estate Debt division. This includes reviewing and approving conditions precedent, reviewing initial loan fundings and construction progress advances, and coordinating the loan funding process with internal and external stakeholders. The Associate Director, Funding has primary responsibility for credit and transactional oversight of the advances that KV Capital funds towards approved investments. The Associate Director, Funding ensures all funding activity is accurately reflected in KV Capital’s systems and investor reporting, and leads continuous improvement in funding controls, processes, and technology.

Responsibilities

Loan Funding & Coordination
Oversee and perform the final review of conditions precedent prior to initial advances for new mortgage loan investments. This includes title, security documents, insurance, appraisals, environmental and geotechnical reports, cost consultant reports, and equity verification.
Review and approve construction progress advance requests within delegated authority. This includes quantity surveyor and cost consultant reports, cost-to-complete recalculations, holdback review, lien searches, and title sub-searches. Loan program "exception" requests and higher-risk advance requests are escalated to the Vice President, Investment Management, where necessary.
Oversee team members responsible for instructing external solicitors, reviewing solicitor reports, and coordinating funding with borrowers, brokers, legal counsel, consultants, and syndicate and institutional partners.
Ensure fundings are executed in accordance with participation, syndication, servicing, and interlender agreements, including timely partner approvals, funding notices, and pro rata advances.
Review funding packages issued to investors, including KV Mortgage Fund, for accuracy and completeness.
Ensure all loan advances are accurately recorded in the system, enabling proper calculation of LTV, LTC, interest reserves, and remaining commitments.
Work with the Capital Markets and Corporate teams to forecast funding requirements and committed undrawn balances for liquidity planning.
Monitor commitment letter conditions and ongoing covenants throughout the funding period, and flag defaults, budget overruns, or adverse changes in project status.

Builder Lines of Credit (BLOC)
Oversee the credit and transactional administration of the BLOC portfolio from approval through renewal and repayment.
Review underwrites prepared by Origination and Investment Management for new BLOC facilities and renewals. Reviews cover:
Builder track record, experience, and capacity;
Corporate financial statements, tax filings, and work-in-progress schedules;
Guarantor net worth, liquidity, and contingent liabilities;
Inventory levels, absorption, and sales history; and
Market conditions in the builder's target geographies and product types.
Review and approve requests to add projects, lots, or units to existing facilities. Each request is assessed against facility terms, including eligible product types and geographies, per-unit and aggregate sub-limits, spec-to-presale ratios, LTV/LTC, budget reasonability, permits, and title.
Review BLOC draw requests against unit-level budgets, cost-to-complete, and margin or borrowing base requirements.
Monitor ongoing facility compliance, including aggregate limits, speculative unit limits, unit aging and maximum hold periods, concentration limits, and reporting covenants. Recommend curtailments, paydowns, or suspension of availability where warranted.
Oversee unit sale repayments, partial discharges, release prices, and re-advances under revolving availability, ensuring net sale proceeds are applied in accordance with facility terms.
Review amendments, extensions, renewals, and annual reviews of BLOC facilities in coordination with Origination and legal counsel.
Conduct or coordinate periodic site visits and inventory inspections for BLOC facilities.
Recommend enhancements to BLOC program guidelines, documentation, and reporting templates based on portfolio performance and market conditions.

Credit Review & Analysis
Review credit applications on an ongoing basis, separately or in conjunction with Funding responsibilities, to evaluate:
Market value reasonability;
Borrower credibility and repayment ability;
Project feasibility and exit strategy viability; and
Market outlook, economic fundamentals, and risk factors.
Review Letters of Interest, Commitment Letters, and amendments to confirm that funding mechanics are clear and administrable, including advance conditions, holdbacks, reserves, and release provisions.
Identify key risks and mitigants in transactions, ensuring appropriate security and documentation structures.
Support the management of high-risk and distressed files by providing funding history, cost-to-complete analysis, and recommendations on protective advances.

Process Improvement & Compliance
Develop, implement, and maintain funding controls, checklists, and approval matrices to enhance accuracy in funding calculations and approvals.
Ensure compliance with company policies, investor guidelines, KV Mortgage Fund Board resolutions, syndicate agreements, and regulatory, legal, and ethical standards related to funding.
Monitor key operational metrics related to funding processes and recommend strategic improvements.

Special Projects & Strategic Initiatives
Lead or participate in initiatives focused on optimizing funding operations, BLOC administration, and credit analysis methodologies.
Support technology and automation enhancements to streamline funding workflows.
Provide insight and recommendations for special projects, including market research and process improvements.
Support the day-to-day operations of the Funding team by providing mentorship, technical guidance, and assistance to Funding Analysts, including support with work prioritization and ongoing training and development.
Drive team engagement and ensure KVC's culture and values are embedded within the Funding team.

Requirements

A bachelor's degree in finance, real estate, economics, business, or a related field is required. Advanced certifications such as CPA, CFA, or MBA are considered an asset.
5+ years of directly related experience in mortgage underwriting, credit analysis, construction lending, or loan administration.
Demonstrated experience with construction draw processes, builder or revolving credit facilities, and funding procedures.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and support the development of team members is considered an asset.
Hold or is working towards being registered as a licensed brokerage associate in the relevant geographical regions for KV's business.
Familiarity with mortgage loan documentation, legal security processes, syndication and interlender arrangements, and applicable regulations.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, with demonstrated expertise in Excel.
Comfort and ability to use, learn, and adapt to new technology and tools supporting business processes and analysis.

Competitive total compensation package, including performance-based and long-term incentives
Eligible to participate in the Employee Stock Option Plan
Comprehensive paid time-off package, including birthdays off and holiday office closures
100% employer-paid benefits
Financial and organizational support for professional development opportunities
Flexible work environment, including hybrid work offering (4 days in office, 1 day remote per week)

We are passionate about our business, our culture and investing deeply in your growth and development to build for the future. You will be part of an enthusiastic and highly effective team with no end to challenging and transformational work in sight. KV Capital is in a phase of growth and expansion, offering a collaborative work environment, recognition for outstanding performance and abundant opportunities for both personal and professional advancement.

Who We Are

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.
Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.
Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our blog and follow us @InsideGeotab on Instagram.

Who You Are

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Head of Tax & Asset Compliance who will own the solution domain that helps North American fleets meet their tax and asset compliance obligations while protecting profitability. If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader — we would love to hear from you!

What You'll Do

As a Head of Tax & Asset Compliance your key area of responsibility will be turning Geotab's telematics data into compliance outcomes (automated evidence, filings, and monitoring) that minimize compliance violations, fines, downtime, and administrative burden. You will need to work closely with the Tech Dev Board, Heads of Platform Domain, Heads of Segment Domain, peer Heads of Solution Domain, cross-functional domain teams (product managers, designers, product engineers), and external fleet customers.
To be successful in this role you will be a strategic leader with deep customer empathy, high adaptability, change readiness, and strong stakeholder management and communication skills. In addition, the successful candidate will have P&L literacy, commercial instinct, expertise in defining and tracking product KPIs, and the ability to operate at the intersection of business strategy, customer experience, and technical execution.

How You'll Make An Impact

Product Strategy & Vision: Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the domain, driving build/buy/partner decisions and evaluating emerging customer needs to strengthen market differentiation .
Business & Metric Ownership: Accountable for primary business KPAs (e.g., submission success rates, violations avoided) and driving adoption of compliance workflows .
Customer Value Delivery: Serve fleet operators, compliance managers, and asset owners as primary customers, defining and measuring experience metrics (adoption, time-to-value, NPS) .
Cross-Segment Alignment: Partner with Heads of Segment Domain to ensure tax and asset compliance capabilities are packaged and positioned effectively for key market segments .
Feedback Loops & Experience Quality: Establish strong feedback loops with customers, sales, and support to resolve product gaps while owning UX quality standards across all domain surfaces .
People Leadership & Coaching: Provide mentoring, career development, and performance management to cross-functional teams, identifying and coaching high-potential, next-generation leaders .
Culture & Capacity Management: Foster a high-trust, high-accountability team culture focused on customer obsession and rapid iteration while managing team capacity across discovery and delivery .
Financial Stewardship & Investment: Own the domain investment portfolio, leading annual planning for budget, headcount, and OKRs while balancing growth, quality, and capability bets .
Executive & Board Reporting: Translate board-level direction into execution plans and regularly report on domain outcomes, revenue contributions, and delivery health to executive leadership .
Cross-Domain & Platform Collaboration: Partner with Heads of Platform Domain to leverage shared infrastructure/APIs and coordinate with peer solution domains to eliminate duplication .
Community & Strategic Leadership: Participate in practitioner communities (Engineering, Product, Design) and lead board-appointed, cross-functional initiatives across domains .
Organizational Strategic Alignment: Support company-wide strategic initiatives, including AI workflow adoption, security posture, accessibility, and compliance pro grams

What You'll Bring To This Role

10+ years of experience in product management, product engineering, or related customer-facing product roles .
5+ years of senior product and people leadership with cross-functional scope and direct accountability for customer-facing business outcomes .
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and work experience) .
Strong product leadership capability with demonstrated ability to define and execute customer-facing product strategy tied to measurable business outcomes, with P&L literacy and revenue attribution .
Cross-functional leadership experience managing teams across product management, product design, and product engineering disciplines, with proven capability in identifying and coaching high-potential leaders .
Excellent stakeholder management, change readiness, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with platform teams, segment leads, and executive leadership in evolving organizational structures .
Familiarity with modern product discovery, validation practices, and engineering practices (CI/CD, cloud-native delivery, agile), alongside the ability to redesign domain workflows around AI to compress effort.

If you got this far, we hope you're feeling excited about this role! Even if you don't feel you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Why Job Seekers Choose Geotab

Flex working arrangements
Baby bonus & parental leave top up program
Online learning and networking opportunities
Electric vehicle purchase incentive program
Competitive medical and dental benefits
Retirement savings program

*The above are offered to full-time permanent employees only

How We Work

At Geotab, we have adopted a flexible hybrid working model in that we have systems, functions, programs and policies in place to support both in-person and virtual work. However, you are welcomed and encouraged to come into our beautiful, safe, clean offices as often as you like. When working from home, you are required to have a reliable internet connection with at least 50mb DL/10mb UL. Virtual work is supported with cloud-based applications, collaboration tools and asynchronous working. The health and safety of employees are a top priority. We encourage work-life balance and keep the Geotab culture going strong with online social events, chat rooms and gatherings. Join us and help reshape the future of technology!

Position Description:
The Toronto Region Board of Trade is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology for a 14-month contract to lead the Board's IT team. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, you will ensure the Board's systems remain secure, reliable and well-supported, and serve as a trusted technology partner across all levels of the organization. This role oversees IT operations, business applications, vendor partnerships, cybersecurity and in-flight technology initiatives within a Microsoft-centred environment that includes Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform. In addition to progressive IT leadership experience, the ideal candidate will be a clear communicator, highly collaborative, and able to step into an established environment quickly, combining sound strategic judgment with a hands-on approach to day-to-day operations.

Technology Leadership & Execution

Serves as the senior technology advisor to the Chief Financial Officer and leadership team, providing clear, concise updates and recommendations.

Ensures technology priorities remain aligned with organizational goals and carries forward in-flight initiatives to agreed milestones.

Maintains a strong understanding of the organization’s technology environment and remains actively involved in the execution and resolution of day-to-day technology matters.

Identifies opportunities to improve technology effectiveness, reliability and user experience, with a focus on practical solutions appropriate for a 50-100-person organization.

AI Implementation & Adoption

Supports the implementation of agentic AI solutions across the organization, working with business teams and external partners to identify practical use cases, configure and test solutions, and integrate them into everyday workflows.

Manages and supports the Board’s AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, overseeing licensing, access, configuration and technical support.

Coordinates the technical requirements for AI implementation, including system integrations, data access, testing and deployment, ensuring appropriate security controls and human oversight in accordance with the Board’s AI use policy.

Provides practical guidance, training and troubleshooting to help employees adopt AI tools and apply them effectively in their work.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Leads, supports and develops the IT team, setting priorities and managing performance and KPIs.

Provides service to all areas of the Board by applying business partner skills and a client service outlook.

Allocates work effectively across the team and ensures appropriate coverage for operational priorities, projects and employee support.

Documents key decisions and changes to support a smooth transition at the end of the contract

Vendor Management, Security & Compliance

Manages the relationships with key technology partners, including the managed services providers; monitors performance and oversees renewals and negotiations.

Leads vendor escalations and ensures unresolved service issues are addressed quickly and effectively.

Maintains the Board's cybersecurity posture across Azure and Microsoft 365, including identity, access and data protection.

Upholds IT policies, including the Board's AI use policy, and supports compliance with accessibility (AODA) and privacy requirements.

IT Operations & Service Delivery

Oversees the reliable day-to-day operation of IT infrastructure and technology services at both the Board’s event space at 100 Queens Quay and corporate office at 21 Melinda, including network connectivity, Wi-Fi, end-user services, collaboration tools and telephony.

Takes a hands-on role in addressing operational issues, troubleshooting escalated concerns and coordinating resolution with internal team members and external vendors.

Manages the IT operating calendar, including renewals, reviews and as needed event support.

Maintains service levels and resolves escalated issues promptly.

Oversees technology onboarding and offboarding, hardware and software provisioning, access management and equipment lifecycle requirements.

Business Applications & Data

Oversees the Board's infrastructure including: CRM, marketing automation, finance, event management system, payments, website and related platforms.

Works directly with business teams and vendors to troubleshoot issues, manage enhancements and ensure systems are configured to support operational requirements.

Coordinates system upgrades, integrations, implementations and changes, ensuring appropriate testing, communication, documentation and employee support.

Supports reporting and analytics through Power BI and champions low-code solutions on the Power Platform where they add value.

Identifies opportunities to automate manual processes, simplify workflows and improve productivity using existing technology.

10+ years of progressive IT experience, including experience leading IT teams.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Strong working knowledge of a Microsoft-centred environment, including Azure, Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365.

Practical experience implementing or supporting AI tools and workflow automation, including technical deployment and employee adoption; experience with agentic AI solutions considered an asset.

Experience managing IT infrastructure, connectivity, audiovisual systems and technology support across multiple locations, including corporate office and event environments.

Proven experience managing managed service providers and external agencies, including contracts and performance.

Solid grounding in cybersecurity practices for a cloud-first organization.

Experience managing an IT budget and reporting to senior executives.

Strong oral and written communication skills; experience explaining technical matters to partners at all levels.

Ability to work cross-functionally and collaboratively with business units.

Experience with Business Central, Power BI, ClickDimensions, CMS considered an asset.

A steady, pragmatic leader who builds trust quickly with a new team

A business partner first, able to translate organizational needs into practical technology solutions

Highly organized and able to navigate competing priorities and deadlines

A self-starter who can work independently from a structured handover

A strong communicator, collaborative with colleagues from all levels and departments

Security-minded, detail-oriented and accountable

Full-time position, hybrid with 3-4 days in office.

May require occasional evening and weekend work for system maintenance or emergencies.

On-call availability for critical system issues.

Compensation & Benefits

Deliver strategic transaction advice - Provide timely XVA pricing and strategic transaction guidance to Sales and Trading, including assessment of counterparty credit, funding, collateral, margin, liquidity, and capital impacts.
Manage risk with discipline - Manage material market, credit spread, jump-to-default, wrong-way, basis, funding, and model risks, and establish effective hedging strategies, particularly during periods of market stress.

new_jobs.description:
About KV Capital

At KV Capital, we have established ourselves as industry leaders in real estate debt and investment, driven by our unwavering commitment to excellent, trusted partnerships, and innovating solutions. Since our founding in 2006, we have expanded our business across three connected areas of service: real estate private equity, real estate lending, and private equity investments in real estate supply chain businesses. Managing a robust portfolio of +$1.8 billion in funded investments, accompanied by +$1 billion in assets under management, our dedicated team of finance experts is driven by a shared goal to cultivate prosperity for our clients, investment partners, and communities. We have office locations in Edmonton, Calgary, and Toronto, and continue to expand our reach nationally.

Real Estate Debt (“RED”)

Since its inception, our Real Estate Debt division has funded and/or advised on $2.5B+ of commercial deals. We provide financing solutions for land, subdivision financing, multi-family, retail, industrial, office, hospitality, mixed-use properties, and specialty financing, such as equity and structured finance deals.

Role Summary

Reporting to the Vice President, Investment Management, the Associate Director, Funding is responsible for the oversight and execution of the Funding function within the Real Estate Debt division. This includes reviewing and approving conditions precedent, reviewing initial loan fundings and construction progress advances, and coordinating the loan funding process with internal and external stakeholders. The Associate Director, Funding has primary responsibility for credit and transactional oversight of the advances that KV Capital funds towards approved investments. The Associate Director, Funding ensures all funding activity is accurately reflected in KV Capital’s systems and investor reporting, and leads continuous improvement in funding controls, processes, and technology.

Responsibilities

Loan Funding & Coordination
Oversee and perform the final review of conditions precedent prior to initial advances for new mortgage loan investments. This includes title, security documents, insurance, appraisals, environmental and geotechnical reports, cost consultant reports, and equity verification.
Review and approve construction progress advance requests within delegated authority. This includes quantity surveyor and cost consultant reports, cost-to-complete recalculations, holdback review, lien searches, and title sub-searches. Loan program "exception" requests and higher-risk advance requests are escalated to the Vice President, Investment Management, where necessary.
Oversee team members responsible for instructing external solicitors, reviewing solicitor reports, and coordinating funding with borrowers, brokers, legal counsel, consultants, and syndicate and institutional partners.
Ensure fundings are executed in accordance with participation, syndication, servicing, and interlender agreements, including timely partner approvals, funding notices, and pro rata advances.
Review funding packages issued to investors, including KV Mortgage Fund, for accuracy and completeness.
Ensure all loan advances are accurately recorded in the system, enabling proper calculation of LTV, LTC, interest reserves, and remaining commitments.
Work with the Capital Markets and Corporate teams to forecast funding requirements and committed undrawn balances for liquidity planning.
Monitor commitment letter conditions and ongoing covenants throughout the funding period, and flag defaults, budget overruns, or adverse changes in project status.

Builder Lines of Credit (BLOC)
Oversee the credit and transactional administration of the BLOC portfolio from approval through renewal and repayment.
Review underwrites prepared by Origination and Investment Management for new BLOC facilities and renewals. Reviews cover:
Builder track record, experience, and capacity;
Corporate financial statements, tax filings, and work-in-progress schedules;
Guarantor net worth, liquidity, and contingent liabilities;
Inventory levels, absorption, and sales history; and
Market conditions in the builder's target geographies and product types.
Review and approve requests to add projects, lots, or units to existing facilities. Each request is assessed against facility terms, including eligible product types and geographies, per-unit and aggregate sub-limits, spec-to-presale ratios, LTV/LTC, budget reasonability, permits, and title.
Review BLOC draw requests against unit-level budgets, cost-to-complete, and margin or borrowing base requirements.
Monitor ongoing facility compliance, including aggregate limits, speculative unit limits, unit aging and maximum hold periods, concentration limits, and reporting covenants. Recommend curtailments, paydowns, or suspension of availability where warranted.
Oversee unit sale repayments, partial discharges, release prices, and re-advances under revolving availability, ensuring net sale proceeds are applied in accordance with facility terms.
Review amendments, extensions, renewals, and annual reviews of BLOC facilities in coordination with Origination and legal counsel.
Conduct or coordinate periodic site visits and inventory inspections for BLOC facilities.
Recommend enhancements to BLOC program guidelines, documentation, and reporting templates based on portfolio performance and market conditions.

Credit Review & Analysis
Review credit applications on an ongoing basis, separately or in conjunction with Funding responsibilities, to evaluate:
Market value reasonability;
Borrower credibility and repayment ability;
Project feasibility and exit strategy viability; and
Market outlook, economic fundamentals, and risk factors.
Review Letters of Interest, Commitment Letters, and amendments to confirm that funding mechanics are clear and administrable, including advance conditions, holdbacks, reserves, and release provisions.
Identify key risks and mitigants in transactions, ensuring appropriate security and documentation structures.
Support the management of high-risk and distressed files by providing funding history, cost-to-complete analysis, and recommendations on protective advances.

Process Improvement & Compliance
Develop, implement, and maintain funding controls, checklists, and approval matrices to enhance accuracy in funding calculations and approvals.
Ensure compliance with company policies, investor guidelines, KV Mortgage Fund Board resolutions, syndicate agreements, and regulatory, legal, and ethical standards related to funding.
Monitor key operational metrics related to funding processes and recommend strategic improvements.

Special Projects & Strategic Initiatives
Lead or participate in initiatives focused on optimizing funding operations, BLOC administration, and credit analysis methodologies.
Support technology and automation enhancements to streamline funding workflows.
Provide insight and recommendations for special projects, including market research and process improvements.
Support the day-to-day operations of the Funding team by providing mentorship, technical guidance, and assistance to Funding Analysts, including support with work prioritization and ongoing training and development.
Drive team engagement and ensure KVC's culture and values are embedded within the Funding team.

Requirements

A bachelor's degree in finance, real estate, economics, business, or a related field is required. Advanced certifications such as CPA, CFA, or MBA are considered an asset.
5+ years of directly related experience in mortgage underwriting, credit analysis, construction lending, or loan administration.
Demonstrated experience with construction draw processes, builder or revolving credit facilities, and funding procedures.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and support the development of team members is considered an asset.
Hold or is working towards being registered as a licensed brokerage associate in the relevant geographical regions for KV's business.
Familiarity with mortgage loan documentation, legal security processes, syndication and interlender arrangements, and applicable regulations.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, with demonstrated expertise in Excel.
Comfort and ability to use, learn, and adapt to new technology and tools supporting business processes and analysis.

What KV Capital Offers

Competitive total compensation package, including performance-based and long-term incentives
Eligible to participate in the Employee Stock Option Plan
Comprehensive paid time-off package, including birthdays off and holiday office closures
100% employer-paid benefits
Financial and organizational support for professional development opportunities
Flexible work environment, including hybrid work offering (4 days in office, 1 day remote per week)

Join us at KV Capital and be part of a dynamic team that is redefining success in the real estate debt and investment landscape. We are passionate about our business, our culture and investing deeply in your growth and development to build for the future. You will be part of an enthusiastic and highly effective team with no end to challenging and transformational work in sight. KV Capital is in a phase of growth and expansion, offering a collaborative work environment, recognition for outstanding performance and abundant opportunities for both personal and professional advancement.
